verses.text: Now Jacob see say grain dey for Egypt, and Jacob talk to im pikin dem say, “Why una dey look one another?
Look, I hear say grain dey for Egypt. Go down dere, and buy for us from dere, so that we go live and no die.”
Joseph ten brothers go down to buy grain from Egypt.
But Benjamin, Joseph brother, Jacob no send am with im brothers, because e talk say, “Maybe harm go happen to am.”
Di pikin dem of Israel come to buy among dem wey come, because di famine dey for di land of Canaan.
Joseph na di governor over di land. Na im dey sell to all di people of di land. Joseph brothers come, and bow down to am with dem faces to di ground.
Joseph see im brothers, and e recognize dem, but e make imself strange to dem, and speak roughly with dem. E talk to dem say, “Wia una come from?” Dem talk say, “From di land of Canaan to buy food.”
Joseph recognize im brothers, but dem no recognize am.
Joseph remember di dreams wey e dream about dem, and e talk to dem say, “Una na spies! Una come to see di nakedness of di land!”
Dem talk to am say, “No, my oga, but your servants come to buy food.
We all na one man pikin dem. We na honest men. Your servants no be spies.”
E talk to dem say, “No, but una come to see di nakedness of di land!”
Dem talk say, “We your servants na 12 brothers, di pikin dem of one man for di land of Canaan. Look, di youngest dey with our papa today, and one no dey again.”
Joseph talk to dem say, “Na wetin I talk to una, say una na spies.
By dis una go dey tested: by di life of Pharaoh, una no go go out from here, except your youngest brother come here.
Send one of una, and make e bring your brother, and una go dey kept for prison, so that una words go dey tested, whether truth dey inside una. Or else, by di life of Pharaoh, surely una na spies.”
E put dem all together for custody three days.
Joseph talk to dem di third day, “Do dis, and live, because I fear God.
If una na honest men, make one of una brothers dey bound for di prison where una dey kept. But una go go, carry grain for di famine of una houses.
Bring your youngest brother to me. So una words go dey verified, and una no go die.” Dem do so.
Dem talk to one another say, “We dey truly guilty concerning our brother, because we see di distress of im soul, when e beg us, and we no listen. Na why dis distress don come on us.”
Reuben answer dem say, “I no talk to una say, ‘No sin against di boy,’ and una no listen? Look, im blood dey required.”
Dem no know say Joseph dey understand dem, because dem get interpreter between dem.
E turn away from dem, and weep. E return to dem, and talk to dem, and take Simeon from among dem, and bind am before dem eyes.
Joseph command dem to fill dem containers with grain, and to restore every man money into im sack, and to give dem food for di way. E do so for dem.
Dem load dem grain on dem donkeys, and go from dere.
As one of dem open im sack to give im donkey feed for di inn, e see im money. Look, e dey for di mouth of im sack.
E talk to im brothers say, “My money don return! Look, e even dey for my sack!” Dem heart fail dem, and dem turn trembling to one another, talk say, “Wetin be dis wey God don do to us?”
Dem come to Jacob dem papa for di land of Canaan, and tell am all wey happen to dem, talk say,
“Di man, di oga of di land, talk roughly to us, and take us for spies of di country.
We talk to am say, ‘We na honest men. We no be spies.
We na 12 brothers, pikin dem of our papa. One no dey again, and di youngest dey with our papa today for di land of Canaan.’
Di man, di oga of di land, talk to us say, ‘By dis I go know say una na honest men: leave one of una brothers with me, take grain for di famine of una houses, and go.
Bring your youngest brother to me. Den I go know say una no be spies, but say una na honest men. So I go deliver una brother to una, and una go trade for di land.’”
E come be say as dem dey empty dem sacks, look, every man bundle of money dey im sack. When dem and dem papa see di bundles of money, dem fear.
Jacob dem papa talk to dem say, “Una don bereave me of my pikin dem. Joseph no dey, Simeon no dey, and una go take Benjamin away. All dis things dey against me.”
Reuben talk to im papa say, “Kill my two pikin man dem, if I no bring am to you. Put am for my hand, and I go bring am to you again.”
E talk say, “My pikin no go go down with una, because im brother don die, and e only remain. If harm happen to am for di way wey una go, una go bring down my grey hair with sorrow to Sheol.”
Di famine severe for di land.
E come be say, when dem don eat up di grain wey dem bring from Egypt, dem papa talk to dem say, “Go again, buy us small food.”
Judah talk to am say, “Di man solemnly warn us, say, ‘Una no go see my face, except your brother dey with una.’
If you go send our brother with us, we go go down and buy you food,
but if you no go send am, we no go go down, because di man talk to us say, ‘Una no go see my face, except your brother dey with una.’”
Israel talk say, “Why una treat me so badly, to tell di man say una still get one brother?”

Dem talk say, “Di man ask carefully about us, and about our relatives, talk say, ‘Your papa still dey alive? Una get another brother?’ We tell am according to dem words. We fit know say e go talk, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
Judah talk to Israel im papa, “Send di boy with me, and we go arise and go, so that we go live and no die, both we, and you, and our little ones.
I go be surety for am. From my hand you go require am. If I no bring am to you, and set am before you, make I bear di blame forever.
Because if we no delay, surely by now we for don return two times.”
Israel dem papa talk to dem, “If na so, do dis: take of di best fruits of di land for your bags, and carry down to di man one present, small balm, small honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds.
Take double money for your hand, and di money wey dem return for di mouth of your sacks, carry am again for your hand. Maybe na mistake.
Take your brother too, arise, and return to di man.
Make God give una mercy before di man, so that e go release to una your other brother and Benjamin. If I dey bereaved of my pikin dem, I dey bereaved.”
Di men take dis present, and dem take double money for dem hand, and Benjamin. Dem rise up, go down to Egypt, and stand before Joseph.
When Joseph see Benjamin with dem, e talk to di steward of im house, “Bring di men home, and kill animal, and make ready, because di men go dine with me at noon.”
Di man do as Joseph talk, and di man bring di men into Joseph house.

Di men fear, because dem bring dem into Joseph house. Dem talk say, “Because of di money wey return for our sacks for di first time, na im dem bring us in, so that e go find occasion against us, fall on us, and take us as slaves, with our donkeys.”
Dem come near to di steward of Joseph house, and dem talk to am for di door of di house,
and talk say, “Oh my oga, we truly come down di first time to buy food.
E come be say, when we come to di inn, we open our sacks, and look, every man money dey for di mouth of im sack, our money for full weight. We don bring am again for our hand.
We don bring down other money for our hand to buy food. We no know who put our money for our sacks.”
E talk say, “Peace dey with una. No fear. Una God, and di God of una papa, don give una treasure for una sacks. I get una money.” E bring Simeon out to dem.
Di man bring di men into Joseph house, and give dem water, and dem wash dem feet. E give dem donkeys feed.
Dem prepare di present against Joseph come at noon, because dem hear say dem go eat bread dere.
When Joseph come home, dem bring di present wey dey dem hand into di house to am, and bow down to am to di earth.
E ask dem about dem welfare, and talk say, “Una papa dey well, di old man wey una talk about? E still dey alive?”
Dem talk say, “Your servant our papa dey well. E still dey alive.” Dem bow down im head, and make obeisance.
E lift up im eyes, and see Benjamin im brother, im mama pikin, and talk say, “Dis na your youngest brother, wey una talk to me about?” E talk say, “God be gracious to you, my pikin.”
Joseph hurry, because im heart yearn for im brother, and e seek where to weep. E enter im room, and weep dere.
E wash im face, and go out. E restrain imself, and talk say, “Serve di food.”
Dem serve am by imself, and dem by demself, and di Egyptians wey dey eat with am by demself, because di Egyptians no fit eat bread with di Hebrews, because dat na abomination to di Egyptians.
Dem sit before am, di firstborn according to im birthright, and di youngest according to im youth, and di men look at one another with wonder.
E send portions to dem from before am, but Benjamin portion pass any of dem five times. Dem drink, and dey merry with am.
E command di steward of im house, talk say, “Fill di men sacks with food, as much as dem fit carry, and put every man money for di mouth of im sack.
Put my cup, di silver cup, for di mouth of di sack of di youngest, with im grain money.” E do according to di word wey Joseph talk.
As soon as morning dey light, dem send di men away, dem and dem donkeys.
When dem don go out of di city, and no far, Joseph talk to im steward, “Up, follow di men. When you overtake dem, talk to dem, ‘Why una don repay evil for good?
Dis na di cup wey my oga dey drink from, and wey e use for divination. Una don do evil for wetin una do.’”
E overtake dem, and e talk to dem dem words.
Dem talk to am say, “Why my oga talk dis kind words? Make e no be say your servants do dis kind thing.
Look, di money wey we find for di mouth of our sacks, we bring am again to you out of di land of Canaan. How then we go steal silver or gold from your oga house?
Whoever of your servants wey dem find am with, make e die, and we too go be my oga slaves.”
E talk say, “Now also make am be according to your words. Im wey dem find am with go be my slave, and una go be blameless.”
Den dem hurry, take down every man im sack to di ground, and open every man im sack.
E search, begin with di oldest, and finish with di youngest. Di cup dey found for Benjamin sack.
Den dem tear dem clothes, and every man load im donkey, and return to di city.
Judah and im brothers come to Joseph house, and e still dey dere. Dem fall on di ground before am.
Joseph talk to dem say, “Wetin be dis deed wey una don do? Una no know say man like me fit really divine?”

Judah talk say, “Wetin we go talk to my oga? Wetin we go speak? Or how we go clear ourselves? God don find out di iniquity of your servants. Look, we na slaves of my oga, both we and im with who dem find di cup.”
E talk say, “Far be am from me say I do so. Di man with who dem find di cup, na im go be my slave. But una, go up in peace to una papa.”
Den Judah come near to am, and talk say, “Oh my oga, make your servant speak one word for my oga ears, and make your anger no burn against your servant, because you dey like Pharaoh.
My oga ask im servants, talk say, ‘Una get papa or brother?’
We talk to my oga, ‘We get one old papa, and one young pikin of im old age. Im brother don die, and e alone remain of im mama, and im papa love am.’
You talk to your servants, ‘Bring am down to me, so that I go set my eyes on am.’
We talk to my oga, ‘Di boy no fit leave im papa, because if e leave im papa, im papa go die.’
You talk to your servants, ‘Except your youngest brother come down with una, una go see my face no more.’
E come be say when we go up to your servant my papa, we tell am di words of my oga.
Our papa talk, ‘Go again, buy us small food.’
We talk, ‘We no fit go down. If our youngest brother dey with us, we go go down, because we no fit see di man face, except our youngest brother dey with us.’
Your servant my papa talk to us, ‘Una know say my wife born me two pikin man dem.
One go out from me, and I talk say surely e don tear to pieces, and I no see am since.
If una take dis one too from me, and harm happen to am, una go bring down my grey hair with sorrow to Sheol.’
Now therefore when I come to your servant my papa, and di boy no dey with us, seeing say im life tie to di boy life,
e go come be say, when e see say di boy no dey, e go die. Your servants go bring down di grey hair of your servant our papa with sorrow to Sheol.
Because your servant become surety for di boy to my papa, talk, ‘If I no bring am to you, make I bear di blame to my papa forever.’
Now therefore, make your servant stay instead of di boy as slave to my oga, and make di boy go up with im brothers.
Because how I go go up to my papa, and di boy no dey with me? I no fit see di evil wey go come on my papa.”
Den Joseph no fit restrain imself before all wey stand by am, and e cry say, “Make everybody go out from me!” No man stand with am, while Joseph make imself known to im brothers.
E weep aloud, and di Egyptians hear, and Pharaoh house hear.
Joseph talk to im brothers say, “I na Joseph! My papa still dey alive?” Im brothers no fit answer am, because dem dey terrified for im presence.
Joseph talk to im brothers say, “Come near to me now.” Dem come near. E talk say, “I na Joseph your brother, wey una sell into Egypt.
Now no dey grieved, nor angry with yourselves, say una sell me here, because God send me before una to preserve life.
Because dis na di second year of di famine for di land, and five years still remain, wey no go get plowing nor harvest.
God send me before una to preserve for una one remnant for di earth, and to save una alive by great deliverance.
So now no be una send me here, but God, and e don make me papa to Pharaoh, and oga of all im house, and ruler over all di land of Egypt.
Hurry, go up to my papa, and talk to am say, ‘Your pikin Joseph talk say God don make am oga of all Egypt. Make you come down to am, no delay.
You go dwell for di land of Goshen, and you go dey near to me, you, and your pikin dem, and your grandpikin dem, and your flocks, and your herds, and all wey you get.
Dere I go provide for you, because five years of famine still remain, so that you no go come to poverty, you, and your household, and all wey you get.’
Look, your eyes see, and di eyes of my brother Benjamin see, say na my mouth dey speak to una.
Una go tell my papa of all my glory for Egypt, and of all wey una don see. Una go hurry and bring my papa down here.”
E fall on im brother Benjamin neck, and weep, and Benjamin weep on im neck.
E kiss all im brothers, and weep on dem. After dat im brothers talk with am.
Di news dey heard for Pharaoh house, say, “Joseph brothers don come.” E good for di eyes of Pharaoh and im servants.
Pharaoh talk to Joseph, “Talk to your brothers, ‘Do dis: load your animals, and go, return to di land of Canaan.
Take your papa and your households, and come to me, and I go give una di good of di land of Egypt, and una go eat di fat of di land.’
Now you dey commanded, ‘Do dis: take wagons out of di land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your papa, and come.
No regret your goods, because di good of all di land of Egypt na yours.’”
Di pikin dem of Israel do so. Joseph give dem wagons, according to Pharaoh command, and give dem provision for di way.
To all of dem e give each man changes of clothing, but to Benjamin e give 300 pieces of silver, and five changes of clothing.
E send to im papa like dis: ten donkeys loaded with di good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provision for im papa for di way.
So e send im brothers away, and dem leave. E talk to dem say, “No quarrel for di way.”
Dem go up out of Egypt, and come to di land of Canaan, to Jacob dem papa.
Dem tell am, say, “Joseph still dey alive, and na im be ruler over all di land of Egypt.” Im heart faint, because e no believe dem.
Dem tell am all di words of Joseph, wey e talk to dem. When e see di wagons wey Joseph send to carry am, di spirit of Jacob dem papa revive.
Israel talk say, “E don enough. Joseph my pikin still dey alive. I go go and see am before I die.”
Israel journey with all wey e get, and come to Beersheba, and offer sacrifices to di God of im papa Isaac.
God talk to Israel for visions of di night, talk say, “Jacob, Jacob!” E talk say, “Here I dey.”
E talk say, “I na God, di God of your papa. No fear to go down into Egypt, because dere I go make you great nation.
I go go down with you into Egypt, and I go surely bring you up again. Joseph go put im hand on your eyes.”
Jacob rise up from Beersheba, and di pikin dem of Israel carry Jacob dem papa, dem little ones, and dem wives, for di wagons wey Pharaoh send to carry am.
Dem take dem livestock, and dem goods, wey dem don get for di land of Canaan, and come into Egypt, Jacob, and all im seed with am:
im pikin man dem, and im grandpikin man dem with am, im pikin woman dem, and im grandpikin woman dem, and all im seed e bring with am into Egypt.
Dis na di names of di pikin dem of Israel, wey come into Egypt, Jacob and im pikin dem: Reuben, Jacob firstborn.
Di pikin dem of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Di pikin dem of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, di pikin of one Canaanite woman.
Di pikin dem of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Di pikin dem of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan die for di land of Canaan. Di pikin dem of Perez na Hezron and Hamul.
Di pikin dem of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
Di pikin dem of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
Dis na di pikin dem of Leah, wey e born to Jacob for Paddan Aram, with im pikin woman Dinah. All di souls of im pikin man dem and im pikin woman dem na 33.
Di pikin dem of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
Di pikin dem of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah, dem sister. Di pikin dem of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
Dis na di pikin dem of Zilpah, wey Laban give to im pikin woman Leah, and dem na wetin e born to Jacob, 16 souls.
Di pikin dem of Rachel, Jacob wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
To Joseph for di land of Egypt, Manasseh and Ephraim born, wey Asenath, di pikin woman of Potiphera, priest of On, born to am.
Di pikin dem of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
Dis na di pikin dem of Rachel, wey dem born to Jacob: 14 souls in all.
Di pikin of Dan: Hushim.
Di pikin dem of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
Dis na di pikin dem of Bilhah, wey Laban give to Rachel im pikin woman, and e born dem to Jacob: seven souls in all.
All di souls wey come with Jacob into Egypt, wey come out of im body, besides Jacob pikin man dem wives, all di souls na 66.
Di pikin dem of Joseph, wey dem born to am for Egypt, na two souls. All di souls of di house of Jacob, wey come into Egypt, na 70.
E send Judah before am to Joseph, to show di way before am to Goshen, and dem come into di land of Goshen.
Joseph make ready im chariot, and go up to meet Israel im papa, to Goshen. E present imself to am, fall on im neck, and weep on im neck for long time.
Israel talk to Joseph say, “Now make I die, since I don see your face, say you still dey alive.”
Joseph talk to im brothers, and to im papa house, “I go go up, and tell Pharaoh, and talk to am, ‘My brothers, and my papa house, wey dey for di land of Canaan, don come to me.
Di men na shepherds, because dem dey keep livestock. Dem don bring dem flocks, dem herds, and all wey dem get.’
E go come be say, when Pharaoh call una, and talk say, ‘Wetin your occupation be?’

Una go talk, ‘Your servants don dey keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our papa dem,’ so that una go dwell for di land of Goshen, because every shepherd na abomination to di Egyptians.”
Den Joseph go in and tell Pharaoh, say, “My papa and my brothers, with dem flocks, dem herds, and all wey dem get, don come out of di land of Canaan. Look, dem dey di land of Goshen.”
From among im brothers e take five men, and present dem to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk to im brothers, “Wetin your occupation be?” Dem talk to Pharaoh say, “Your servants na shepherds, both we, and our papa dem.”

Dem talk to Pharaoh say, “We don come to sojourn for di land, because no pasture dey for your servants flocks, because di famine severe for di land of Canaan. Now therefore, make your servants dwell for di land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh talk to Joseph say, “Your papa and your brothers don come to you.

Di land of Egypt dey before you. Make your papa and your brothers dwell for di best of di land. Make dem dwell for di land of Goshen. If you know any capable men among dem, make dem rulers over my livestock.”
Joseph bring Jacob im papa in, and set am before Pharaoh. Jacob bless Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk to Jacob, “How many na di days of di years of your life?”

Jacob talk to Pharaoh say, “Di days of di years of my sojourning na 130 years. Few and evil don be di days of di years of my life, and dem no reach di days of di years of my papa dem for di days of dem sojourning.”
Jacob bless Pharaoh, and go out from before Pharaoh.
Joseph place im papa and im brothers, and give dem possession for di land of Egypt, for di best of di land, for di land of Rameses, as Pharaoh command.
Joseph nourish im papa, im brothers, and all im papa house, with bread, according to dem families.
Dem no get bread for all di land, because di famine very severe, so that di land of Egypt and di land of Canaan faint because of di famine.
Joseph gather up all di money wey dem find for di land of Egypt, and for di land of Canaan, for di grain wey dem buy, and Joseph bring di money into Pharaoh house.
When di money don finish for di land of Egypt and for di land of Canaan, all di Egyptians come to Joseph, talk say, “Give us bread, because why we go die before you? Because di money don finish.”
Joseph talk say, “Give your livestock, and I go give you for your livestock, if di money don finish.”
Dem bring dem livestock to Joseph, and Joseph give dem bread in exchange for di horses, and di flocks, and di herds, and di donkeys. E feed dem with bread for all dem livestock for dat year.

When dat year end, dem come to am di second year, and talk to am say, “We no go hide am from my oga how our money don finish. Di herds of livestock belong to my oga. Nothing remain before my oga except our bodies and our lands.

Why we go die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land go be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, so that we go live and no die, and di land no go be desolate.”
So Joseph buy all di land of Egypt for Pharaoh, because di Egyptians sell every man im field, because di famine strong on dem, and di land become Pharaoh own.
As for di people, e remove dem to di cities from one end of di border of Egypt even to di other end of am.
Only di land of di priests e no buy, because di priests get portion from Pharaoh, and dem dey eat dem portion wey Pharaoh give dem. Na why dem no sell dem land.
Den Joseph talk to di people, “Look, I don buy una and una land today for Pharaoh. Look, here dey seed for una, and una go sow di land.

E go come be say for di harvests, una go give di fifth part to Pharaoh, and four parts go be your own, for seed of di field, and for your food, and for una households, and for food for una little ones.”
Dem talk say, “You don save our lives. Make us find favour for di sight of my oga, and we go be Pharaoh servants.”
Joseph make am law over di land of Egypt to dis day, say Pharaoh must get di fifth part. Only di land of di priests alone no become Pharaoh own.
Israel dwell for di land of Egypt, for di land of Goshen. Dem get possessions dere, and dem born plenty pikin, and multiply greatly.
Jacob live for di land of Egypt 17 years. So di days of Jacob, di years of im life, na 147 years.

Di time draw near wey Israel must die. E call im pikin Joseph, and talk to am say, “If now I don find favour for your sight, put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Make you no bury me for Egypt,
but when I lie with my papa dem, you go carry me out of Egypt, and bury me for dem burying place.” E talk say, “I go do as you don talk.”
E talk say, “Swear to me.” E swear to am. Israel bow imself on di bed head.
E come be say after dis things, one tell Joseph say, “Look, your papa dey sick.” E take with am im two pikin man dem, Manasseh and Ephraim.
One tell Jacob say, “Look, your pikin Joseph dey come to you,” and Israel strengthen imself, and sit up on di bed.
Jacob talk to Joseph, “God Almighty appear to me for Luz for di land of Canaan, and bless me,
and talk to me, ‘Look, I go make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I go make you company of peoples, and go give dis land to your seed after you for everlasting possession.’
Now your two pikin man dem, wey dem born to you for di land of Egypt before I come to you into Egypt, dem na mine. Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, go be mine.
Your offspring, wey you born after dem, go be your own. Dem go dey called by di name of dem brothers for dem inheritance.
As for me, when I come from Paddan, Rachel die by me for di land of Canaan for di way, when e still dey some distance to come to Ephrath, and I bury am dere for di way to Ephrath, wey na Bethlehem.”
Israel see Joseph pikin dem, and talk, “Who be dem?”
Joseph talk to im papa, “Dem na my pikin dem, wey God don give me for dis place.” E talk say, “Bring dem to me, and I go bless dem.”
Now Israel eyes dim for old age, so that e no fit see. E bring dem near to am, and e kiss dem, and embrace dem.
Israel talk to Joseph, “I no think say I go see your face, and look, God don show me your seed too.”
Joseph bring dem out from between im knees, and e bow imself with im face to di earth.
Joseph take dem both, Ephraim with im right hand toward Israel left hand, and Manasseh with im left hand toward Israel right hand, and bring dem near to am.
Israel stretch out im right hand, and lay am on Ephraim head, wey be di younger, and im left hand on Manasseh head, guiding im hands knowingly, because Manasseh na di firstborn.
E bless Joseph, and talk, “Di God before who my papa dem Abraham and Isaac walk, di God wey don feed me all my life long to dis day,
di angel wey don redeem me from all evil, bless di boys. Make my name dey named for dem, and di name of my papa dem Abraham and Isaac. Make dem grow into multitude for di middle of di earth.”
When Joseph see say im papa lay im right hand on Ephraim head, e no good for im eyes. E hold im papa hand, to remove am from Ephraim head to Manasseh head.
Joseph talk to im papa, “No be so, my papa, because dis na di firstborn. Put your right hand on im head.”
Im papa refuse, and talk, “I know, my pikin, I know. E too go become people, and e too go be great. But truly im younger brother go be greater pass am, and im seed go become multitude of nations.”
E bless dem dat day, talk say, “By you Israel go bless, talk say, ‘Make God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.’” E set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Israel talk to Joseph, “Look, I dey die, but God go dey with una, and bring una again to di land of una papa dem.
Moreover I don give to you one portion pass your brothers, wey I take out of di hand of di Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”
Jacob call im pikin man dem, and talk, “Gather yourselves together, so that I go tell una wetin go happen to una for di days to come.
Gather yourselves together, and hear, una pikin dem of Jacob. Listen to Israel una papa.
Reuben, you na my firstborn, my might, and di beginning of my strength, di pre-eminence of dignity, and di pre-eminence of power.
Boiling over like water, you no go excel, because you go up to your papa bed. Den you defile am. E go up to my couch.
Simeon and Levi na brothers. Weapons of violence dey dem swords.
My soul, no come into dem council. My glory, no join dem assembly, because for dem anger dem kill man, and for dem self-will dem hamstring ox.
Cursed be dem anger, because e fierce, and dem wrath, because e cruel. I go divide dem for Jacob, and scatter dem for Israel.
Judah, your brothers go praise you. Your hand go dey for di neck of your enemies. Your papa pikin dem go bow down before you.
Judah na lion cub. From di prey, my pikin, you don go up. E stoop down, e crouch as lion, and as lioness. Who go rouse am up?
Di sceptre no go depart from Judah, nor di ruler staff from between im feet, until Shiloh come. To am di obedience of di peoples go be.
Binding im foal to di vine, and im donkey colt to di choice vine, e don wash im garments for wine, and im robes for di blood of grapes.
Im eyes go be red with wine, and im teeth white with milk.
Zebulun go dwell at di haven of di sea. E go be haven of ships. Im border go be toward Sidon.
Issachar na strong donkey, lying down between di sheepfolds.
E see say rest good, and di land pleasant. E bow im shoulder to di burden, and become servant to taskwork.
Dan go judge im people, as one of di tribes of Israel.
Dan go be serpent for di way, adder for di path, wey bite di horse heels, so that im rider fall backward.
I don wait for your salvation, Lord.
Gad, raiders go raid am, but im go raid dem for dem heels.
Out of Asher, im bread go be fat, and e go yield royal dainties.
Naphtali na doe wey dem set free, wey give beautiful words.
Joseph na fruitful vine, fruitful vine by one spring. Im branches run over di wall.
Di archers don bitterly grieve am, shoot at am, and hate am.
But im bow abide strong, and di arms of im hands dey made strong by di hands of di Mighty One of Jacob, from dere, di Shepherd, di Stone of Israel,
even by di God of your papa, wey go help you, and by di Almighty, wey go bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of di deep wey lie beneath, blessings of di breasts, and of di womb.

Di blessings of your papa don prevail above di blessings of my ancestors, to di utmost bound of di eternal hills. Dem go dey on di head of Joseph, and on di crown of di head of im wey dey separate from im brothers.
Benjamin na wolf wey tear. For di morning e go devour di prey, and for di evening e go divide di spoil.”
All dis na di 12 tribes of Israel, and dis na wetin dem papa talk to dem, and bless dem. E bless dem, everyone according to im blessing.
E command dem, and talk to dem, “I go dey gathered to my people. Bury me with my papa dem for di cave wey dey di field of Ephron di Hittite,
for di cave wey dey di field of Machpelah, wey dey before Mamre, for di land of Canaan, wey Abraham buy with di field from Ephron di Hittite for possession of burying place.
Dere dem bury Abraham and Sarah im wife. Dere dem bury Isaac and Rebekah im wife, and dere I bury Leah.
Di field and di cave wey dey inside, wey dem buy from di pikin dem of Heth.”
When Jacob don finish to command im pikin man dem, e gather up im feet into di bed, and e die, and e join im people.
Joseph fall on im papa face, weep on am, and kiss am.
Joseph command im servants di physicians to embalm im papa, and di physicians embalm Israel.
40 days dey fulfilled for am, because so many days dey fulfilled for embalming. Di Egyptians mourn for am 70 days.
When di days of mourning for am don pass, Joseph talk to Pharaoh house, say, “If now I don find favour for your eyes, make una speak for Pharaoh ears say,
‘My papa make me swear say e dey die, and say make I bury am for im grave wey e don dig for di land of Canaan. Now make I go up, and bury my papa, and I go return.’”
Pharaoh talk say, “Go up, and bury your papa, as e make you swear.”
Joseph go up to bury im papa. All Pharaoh servants, di elders of im house, and all di elders of di land of Egypt go up with am,
and all Joseph house, im brothers, and im papa house. Only dem little ones, and dem flocks and dem herds, dem leave for di land of Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen go up with am too. E be very great company.
Dem come to di threshing floor of Atad, wey dey beyond di Jordan, and dere dem mourn with great and very sore lamentation. E mourn for im papa seven days.

When di inhabitants of di land, di Canaanites, see di mourning for di threshing floor of Atad, dem talk say, “Dis na grievous mourning to di Egyptians.” Na why dem call di name of am Abel Mizraim, wey dey beyond di Jordan.
Im pikin man dem do to am as e command dem,

because im pikin man dem carry am into di land of Canaan, and bury am for di cave of di field of Machpelah, wey Abraham buy with di field for possession of burying place from Ephron di Hittite, before Mamre.
Joseph return into Egypt, e, and im brothers, and all wey go up with am to bury im papa, after e don bury im papa.
When Joseph brothers see say dem papa don die, dem talk say, “Maybe Joseph go hate us, and go pay us back for all di evil wey we do to am.”
Dem send word to Joseph, say, “Your papa command before e die, say,

‘Make una talk to Joseph say make e forgive di disobedience of im brothers, and dem sin, because dem do evil to am.’ Now make you forgive di disobedience of di servants of di God of your papa.” Joseph weep when dem speak to am.
Im brothers come and fall down before im face. Dem talk say, “Look, we be your servants.”
Joseph talk to dem say, “No fear, because I dey God place?
As for una, una mean evil against me, but God mean am for good, to bring am to pass, as e dey today, to save plenty people alive.
Now therefore no fear. I go provide for una and una little ones.” E comfort dem, and speak kindly to dem.
Joseph dwell for Egypt, e, and im papa house. Joseph live 110 years.
Joseph see Ephraim pikin dem to di third generation. Di pikin dem of Machir too, di pikin of Manasseh, dem born on Joseph knees.
Joseph talk to im brothers say, “I dey die, but God go surely visit una, and bring una up out of dis land to di land wey e swear to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
Joseph take oath of di pikin dem of Israel, talk say, “God go surely visit una, and una go carry up my bones from here.”
So Joseph die, being 110 years old. Dem embalm am, and dem put am for coffin for Egypt.
